subject: Procurement path & PR setup for Acme — next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Summers <jill.summers@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement path & PR setup for Acme — next steps

Hi Jill — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps so procurement can move forward.

Summary of the call:
- Goal: Start a pilot integration with Acme for 3 internal teams (search, docs, CX).
- Timeline: target contract signature and provisioning in Q3.
- Commercial path: Acme likely needs to go via PO / PR (not card) — you mentioned finance prefers a PO. We discussed marketplace as a fallback if procurement wants that route.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Confirm whether you prefer us to set up as a marketplace purchase (AWS Marketplace/GCP Marketplace) or via your PO process.
2) If PO path: please confirm the billing contact, cost center, and whether your Coupa or Ariba instance is used for supplier onboarding.
3) If you can share your standard PR form or supplier onboarding checklist, we’ll map required fields to our supplier setup flow.

I’ve attached a short sample PR form and a supplier-setup checklist that our procurement team prefers (attached: sample_pr_form.pdf, supplier_setup_instructions.docx).

I’m looping in Marissa (Finance Ops) and Dylan (Solutions) to advise on PR creation and supplier-ID mapping in Coupa/Ariba — they’ll also create an internal ticket to sequence the work.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the billing contact and whether Acme will use PO vs marketplace.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Jill Summers <jill.summers@acme-corp.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement path & PR setup for Acme — next steps

Thanks, Aisha — appreciated the summary. A few quick notes and a couple of questions from procurement here.

- We will likely go PO for the pilot (Finance wants invoice/PO trail).
- We use Coupa for supplier onboarding.

Questions:
1) What information does Redwood need to create a vendor in Coupa (legal name, W-9, remit address etc.)? Any specific fields we should send in the PR to help Finance map the charge?
2) Do you have a preferred vendor name or supplier ID we should reference in our PR?
3) Can the marketplace route be used in parallel if Coupa onboarding takes longer?

If you can flag who to include from your side (contact for supplier setup + procurement contact), I’ll share details with our AP team and get a PO template over.

Best,
Jill Summers
Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Summers <jill.summers@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Looping procurement ops & PR guidance — Acme pilot (RDW-4532)

Hi Jill / Acme procurement — looping in Marissa (Finance Ops) and Dylan (Solutions) to provide concrete guidance for PR creation and supplier ID mapping in Coupa.

High-level ask from Acme: PO path preferred; uses Coupa; will share PO/PR template. Below are the items we typically require to accelerate vendor setup and avoid back-and-forth:

Required for supplier onboarding / PR: 
- Legal entity name (as on W-9 / tax docs)
- Remit address + invoice email
- Billing contact name, phone, and email
- Expected billing cadence (monthly/quarterly) and initial invoice amount range
- Preferred vendor name to appear on PR (e.g., "Redwood Inference, Inc.")
- Internal cost center / GL code (if available) to include on PR

Coupa/Ariba specifics we need to confirm:
- Whether Acme requires a Supplier ID pre-created before PR (some teams want a Supplier ID in Coupa tied to a vendor record; others allow a PR to create a request and then map the invoice after onboarding)
- Any required field mapping (cost center, project code, approver chain) — please attach your PR form so we can pre-populate our onboarding packet.

Attachments: sample_pr_form.pdf (example fields we ask for), supplier_setup_instructions.docx (internal checklist).

Marissa / Dylan — can you confirm the exact vendor name we prefer and the fields our finance team will require to accept a PO (and whether we can accept a PR referencing a pending supplier request)? Also please advise the internal ticketing we’ll open so Acme can reference it.

Thanks,
Aisha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Jill Summers <jill.summers@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Looping procurement ops & PR guidance — Acme pilot (RDW-4532)

Hi all — thanks for the context. Here’s the operational guidance to make PR creation and supplier linkage in Coupa/Ariba straightforward.

1) Preferred vendor identity: 
- Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Tax ID and W-9 available upon request (I can attach once Acme confirms supplier email).

2) PR fields that speed processing (please include these in the PR form):
- Line items: "Redwood Inference — LLM inference pilot" (short description)
- Qty: 1, Unit price: enter estimated monthly commit or initial one-time professional services amount
- Account/GL: If Acme needs a default, our default GL for SaaS is 6100 (software subscriptions) — we can map if you use different codes
- Cost center / project code: include if available to avoid routing delays

3) Supplier record / Supplier ID: 
- Coupa: Many Acme teams create a supplier-request PR that references a temporary placeholder supplier name; Coupa will create a supplier ID after AP reviews vendor docs. That works for most customers.
- Ariba: Ariba often requires an existing supplier record before PO issuance — if you’re on Ariba we’ll prioritize W-9 and banking details to speed registration.

4) Documents to attach when creating a PR or supplier request:
- Signed SOW or purchase description (if available)
- Our W-9 (will provide when you confirm vendor email)
- Supplier contact email for invoicing: finance-invoices@redwood.ai

5) Internal ticketing & SLA:
- I’ve opened an internal procurement ticket to track Acme onboarding: JIRA AP-23456 (link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/AP-23456).
- Target internal SLA: supplier record created and PO accepted within 5–7 business days after Acme returns completed vendor docs.

If you want, we can also provide a marketplace invoice in parallel as a short-term fallback — note that marketplace purchases may have different billing terms and may not align with your PO process.

Attachments included: sample_pr_form.pdf, supplier_setup_instructions.docx.

Happy to jump on a quick 15-min call with Acme AP to walk through the Coupa flow if that’s helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Finance Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jill — and thanks Marissa for the clear steps. 

Jill / Acme AP — next actions from our side and timeline: 
- We will provide the W-9 and Redwood vendor packet to you by end of day today once you confirm the supplier email to send to.
- Marissa has opened JIRA AP-23456 to track the onboarding work; I’ll add the HubSpot deal (RDW-4532) link there for reference.
- If you confirm the PO route, please create the supplier-request PR in Coupa and reference "Redwood Inference, Inc." and include your cost center / project code. If Coupa allows a PR that triggers supplier creation, we’ll accept invoices against the PR while supplier record is finalized.

Can you confirm the supplier email to send W-9 and whether you want us to initiate a marketplace invoice in parallel? Once I get your confirmation I’ll:
1) Upload W-9 to the JIRA ticket and tag your AP contact
2) Share expected invoice templates
3) Schedule a 15-min walkthrough with your AP team if useful

Thanks — looking forward to getting the PR in place so you can onboard the pilot.

Best regards,
Aisha Rahman
